Setting it beside two wrongs against others (ஆற்றானை ஆற்றென்று அலைப்பான், ஏற்றார்க்கு இயைவ கரப்பான்) is exactly what list_adds says.

Both name Paari and Kapilar and the kings' siege: வாய்மொழிக் கபிலன் சூழ ... வேந்தர் ஓட்டிய ... பாரி (Akam 78), and Kapilar's மூவிரும் முற்றினும் to the kings at Parambu (Puram 109). Teaches is accurate that the Akam poem uses the siege as settled fame to praise the girl's brow.

பெண்மை நலத்துக்கு அணியென்ப நாணம் and the Kural's அணிஅன்றோ நாணுடைமை சான்றோர்க்கு share அணி and நாண். Teaches describes the narrowing to women as a norm the text states, without endorsing it. List_adds is false on the Kural side: the couplet also calls நாண் an அணி, an ornament, so the contrast with 'a guard of conduct' does not hold.

பேரில் பிறந்தமை ஈரத்தின் அறிப and the Kural's குலத்தில் பிறந்தார்வாய்ச் சொல் share one form, birth known by a sign, so this is a parallel more than a qualification. List_adds is true (verse 12: ஈரம் உடைமை ஈகையின் அறிப). But teaches' 'harder to counterfeit' is a claim neither text makes.
links.text_issue: The packet flags that the site lacks line 2.

verses.note: Five passing things (youth goes, disease and age come, wealth and strength fade) precede the counsel to seek வீடு; the counsel is not counted, so the count is 5.
வேதம் and வேள்வி are only the standards of comparison; the verse states no ritual rule.
Lines 1-2 are hard to divide, so the five arts are held loosely.
குலம் is named as a worldly pride that keeps people from renouncing in youth, not as a birth rule, so I gave it no norm.
There is no count word; the five are read from line 1 and தேன் in line 2.
Two of the three items are renunciatory (youth seen as age, women seen as poison), so I gave ascetic.
Three of the five address the household (wife, son, kin) and two the king's realm (soldier, country).
I took 'not trusting women's words' as a gender norm.
Line 1 lists what joining those without சால்பு costs, and line 3 its six fruits; I counted the six fruits.
The count word ஏழு gives seven hells, not the 6 or 5 expected for Elathi; the division of line 2 is uncertain.
These are a student's rules of hair and bodily conduct; lines 1-2 are obscure.
